decisions.why: exquírere → procurar (row, open; 26:8 exquisívit te fácies mea → a minha face vos procurou), kept apart from quǽrere → buscar. ἐξεζήτησα. MS1932 'busquei a Deus' merges it with quǽrere.

The Latin colon has no verb: 'with my hands, by night, before him'. contra here is the Greek ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ, 'facing, in the presence of' — not hostility; Portuguese 'contra ele' would say 'against him'. DRB supplies 'lifted up to him', MS1932 'estendi as minhas mãos de noite para ele': both add a verb the Latin does not have. The verbless phrase is kept (rule 2: no explaining); 'diante dele' is the plain Portuguese of ἐναντίον.

options.label: diante dele
options.note: Ruling: verbless, as the Latin; ἐναντίον.

options.label: voltadas para ele
options.note: Makes the gesture visible with a participle; still no finite verb.

options.label: estendidas para ele
options.note: The supplied gesture of DRB and MS1932.

decisions.why: consolári is passive in sense here (παρακληθῆναι, 'to be comforted'), as 118:52 et consolátus sum → 'e fui consolado'. The passive is kept; MS1932's reflexive 'recusou consolar-se' makes the soul refuse to comfort itself. Natural order puts the subject first; the Latin's verb-first order is the option. rénuere → recusar (L&S '= recusare').

options.label: A minha alma recusou ser consolada

decisions.why: delectári → deleitar-se (row, settled D44 from 50:18). The Greek here is εὐφράνθην, the verb the Latin usually renders lætári (→ alegrar-se), so D15's Greek test would allow 'alegrei-me'; but the Latin chose delectári, and its row is followed. MS1932 'senti-me cheio de gozo' paraphrases.

Three forms of one Latin verb family, all the Greek ἀδολεσχέω (ἠδολέσχησα, ἠδολέσχουν, ἀδολεσχήσω) — the verb behind 118:15, 23, 27, 48, 78 (→ 'me exercitarei', 'se exercitava') and the noun of 54:3 (exercitátio → exercício). The row exercéri → exercitar-se is followed in all three places, so the psalm's own repetition stays audible. It stands beside meditári each time (76:4 memor fui … exercitátus; 76:7 meditátus … exercitábar; 76:13 meditábor … exercébor), which is why it cannot be 'meditar'. Cost: a blind reader of 54:3 heard bodily exercise; 'ocupar-se' is the row's option. MS1932 varies it (meditei, reflectia, considerarei).

options.label: me exercitei · me exercitava · me exercitarei
me ocupei · me ocupava · me ocuparei
refleti · refletia · refletirei
options.note: MS1932's 76:7 verb; mental, as the context; loses the row.

decisions.why: The prævenire row (118:147–148 'adiantar-se') keeps 'antecipar' for anticipáre, naming this verse. L&S cites it: anticipáre with the accusative, 'to take before the time'. The eyes were awake before the night watches (φυλακάς) came round. The subject is put first, as Portuguese orders it. DRB 'My eyes prevented the watches'; MS1932 'Adiantaram-se às vigílias os meus olhos' (prævenire's verb).

options.label: anteciparam as vigílias
options.note: Ruling: the cognate the prævenire row reserves for this verse.

decisions.why: μετὰ τῆς καρδίας μου: the heart as a companion in the night's talk. 'com o meu coração' keeps the preposition; MS1932 'em meu coração' makes the heart the place.

options.label: com o meu coração
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's cum; DRB 'with my own heart'.

decisions.why: Only here in the psalter. Two readings: 'I swept my spirit' (DRB; scopa, a broom — and 'scopáre' is Isaiah 14:23's sweeping), and 'I searched my spirit' (L&S s.v. scopo¹ = σκοπέω, 'to investigate, test, search: spiritum suum, Vulg. Psa. 76,7'). The form decides for the second: scopébam is an -ēbam imperfect, which the first-conjugation 'scopáre, to sweep' would make scopábam; and the Greek ἔσκαλλεν ('dug, searched') is a searching verb. 'examinar' is the plainest Portuguese of it (scrutári keeps 'sondar', its row). The sweep stays as the option, since it is DRB's image and the traditional English. MS1932 'atormentava' paraphrases. Both Latinist runs (minor) asked 'varria'; held for the reason above, which neither run answered (both derived the verb from scopae without regard to the -ēbam form).

options.label: examinava
options.note: Ruling: L&S, the -ēbam form, the Greek.

decisions.why: proícere → lançar (row; 'lançar fora' at 16:11 with no source); the row names this verse. The Latin and the Greek (ἀπώσεται) give it no object; MS1932 supplies 'abandonar-nos', which decides who is cast off. The object is not supplied (rule 2). numquid → acaso (row). in ætérnum → para sempre (D23).

options.label: lançará fora
options.note: Ruling: the row, no object, as the Latin.

options.label: rejeitará (the stylist)
options.note: The v1 stylist asked it (object-less 'lançará fora' hangs; '-ra pa-'); held for the row — see audit.

decisions.latin: aut non appónet ut complacítior sit adhuc?
decisions.why: appónere + ut: 'add to be', the Hebraism for doing again (προσθήσει τοῦ εὐδοκῆσαι ἔτι). 'tornar a' is how Portuguese says 'do again', and keeps adhuc as 'ainda'. complacítior, comparative of the participle 'well pleased' (εὐδοκῆσαι) → 'mais favorável' (DRB 'more favourable'). The literal 'acrescentar' is kept as the option; MS1932 'não se mostrará mais inclinado a aplacar-se' explains. v2: 'voltar a' for 'tornar a' (the stylist), the same idiom, plainer.

options.label: voltará ainda a ser mais favorável

forms.apponet: voltará ainda a ser mais favorável

options.note: v2: the stylist — 'voltar a' is the current auxiliary of repetition.

options.label: tornará ainda a ser mais favorável

forms.apponet: tornará ainda a ser mais favorável

options.label: voltará ainda a ser mais propício

forms.apponet: voltará ainda a ser mais propício

options.note: Another verb of repetition; propício for complacítior.

decisions.latin: Aut in finem misericórdiam suam abscíndet
decisions.why: in finem (εἰς τέλος) → para sempre where it says perpetuity (row, D27); here the next colon, 'de geração em geração', makes it duration. D27 keeps in finem apart from in ætérnum by row, and the psalm has in ætérnum in the verse before: the two Latin phrases become one Portuguese phrase in neighbouring verses. 'até o fim' (48:9, 17:36b) is the option; it is not negated here, so D27's misreading does not arise, but it can be heard as 'completely'. abscíndere → cortar (ἀποκόψει, 'cut off'), the concrete verb; MS1932 'privar-nos' explains. v2: both readers asked 'até o fim' so that the Latin's move from in ætérnum to in finem is heard; taken, and the phrase moved after the verb (the stylist's order).

options.label: até o fim
options.note: v2: the Latinist and the stylist, independently — keeps in finem apart from 76:8's in ætérnum (48:9's build); not negated, so D27's misreading does not arise.

decisions.latin: aut continébit in ira sua misericórdias suas?
decisions.why: continére, 'hold together, hold in' (συνέξει). The cognate 'conter' says 'hold back, restrain' and keeps the image of the mercies held in inside the wrath. DRB 'shut up'; MS1932 'deterá'. The plural misericórdias is kept, as the Latin and Greek have it.

cœpi is a perfect (ἠρξάμην, aorist). 'Agora comecei' keeps it; MS1932 'Agora começo (a compreender)' turns it to a present and glosses. The object of the beginning is left unsaid, as the Latin leaves it. v2: the subject 'eu' supplied (grammar): without it the stylist and the ambiguity reader both heard 'and he said' (God).

Excélsus as a divine name (also 77:17 in iram excitavérunt Excélsum, 81:6 fílii Excélsi — grep). The Greek is ὕψιστος, Altíssimus's word; D43 kept the adjective excélsus → excelso apart from Altíssimus all the same, and the noun follows it. déxtera → a direita (row). mutátio → mudança (54:20b). DRB and MS1932 'the most High'. v1: the stylist found 'Excelso' precious beside the usual 'Altíssimo', and the ambiguity reader listed it unknown (as the Ps 46 reader did 'excelso'); held under D43, flagged in the row for Gustavo.

options.label: Altíssimo
options.note: The Greek's word; DRB, MS1932; the name Brazilian ears know.

decisions.latin: quia memor ero ab inítio mirabílium tuórum
decisions.why: ab inítio stands between the verb and the genitive, so it can be 'from the beginning I will remember your wonders' or 'the wonders you have done from the beginning' (the Greek the same: ἀπὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν θαυμασίων σου). The Latin's order keeps both open. inítio → início (row, 118:152, 160). DRB 'thy wonders from the beginning' and MS1932 'maravilhas de outrora' take the second.

options.label: das vossas maravilhas desde o início

forms.abinitio: das vossas maravilhas desde o início

options.note: v2: the stylist — the verb reaches its complement first; 'desde o início' at the end can still go with 'me lembrarei' or with 'maravilhas', so the Latin's two readings stay open.

options.label: desde o início das vossas maravilhas

forms.abinitio: desde o início das vossas maravilhas

options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's order; the ear stumbles on 'o início das vossas maravilhas'.

decisions.why: adinvéntio → invenções (row, open, from 27:4), which names this verse as the test: God's own devisings (ἐπιτηδεύμασιν, 'pursuits, doings'). 'invenções' keeps the one word for the six places, the good and the bad; said of God it may sound odd. MS1932 'desígnios' is consílium's word (D33). DRB 'inventions'. v1: the stylist named 76:13 the worst line for 'invenções' (gadgets, fabrications) and the ambiguity reader listed it unknown / odd. Held: the row serves six places, three of them bad devisings; the one plain alternative (desígnios) is taken. Flagged in the row for Gustavo.

options.label: obras engenhosas
options.note: Explains; and 'obras' is ópera's word in the same verse.

options.label: desígnios
options.note: MS1932, and the v1 stylist's request; consílium's word (D33).

decisions.why: The row sancta / sanctum (a place) names 76:14 among the places where in sancto 'is not always a place'. Here the psalm itself answers: 76:20 'In mari via tua' sets the way in the sea as 76:14 sets it in sancto, so the neuter is read as a place, the holy place — DRB 'Thy way, O God, is in the holy place'; 21:4 and 62:3 'no lugar santo'. Ps 59:8 went the other way ('no seu santo', v2) because there nothing in the verse pointed to a place. Both verses are verbless in the Latin and are left verbless (a copula 'está' was tried and dropped: +5 syllables, and the nominal sentence is sayable), so the two verses stay alike in build as the Latin has them. The first half stands alone as a versicle (Psalmi matutinum: 'V. Deus, in sancto via tua. R. Quis Deus magnus sicut Deus noster'). MS1932 'O teu caminho, ó Deus, é santo' paraphrases (and is the Hebrew's sense). v2: the Latinist (minor) marked 'lugar' as choosing one reading of ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ; that is right under rule 2 (keep ambiguities), as at 59:8, so the bare 'no santo' is taken. Cost: 76:20 stays verbless while 76:14 has 'está'.

options.label: no santo está
options.note: v2: the Latinist — the bare neuter, place or holiness left open (59:8's v2 ruling); the copula supplied because 'no santo' alone, verbless, is too cryptic to stand as a versicle.

options.label: no lugar santo
options.note: Draft 1: the row; 76:20's parallel; DRB. The ambiguity reader heard the sanctuary.

options.label: na santidade
options.note: Holiness, the other reading; closes the place.

options.label: no lugar santo está
options.note: The copula supplied (D2 allows it); longer.

decisions.why: A verbless colon: 'a multitude of the sound of waters' (πλῆθος ἤχους ὑδάτων). sónitus → estrondo (9:7b cum sónitu → com estrondo). multitúdo → multidão is the row, but 'a multidão do estrondo' is heard as a crowd; of a mass noun the Latin's multitude is a great quantity, which Portuguese says with 'muito' — a noun becomes an adjective, grammar under D2, with nothing added. The row's literal is the first option. DRB and MS1932 'Great was the noise' / 'Foi grande o estrondo' supply a verb and turn quantity into size. v2: the stylist heard 'Muito estrondo' as colloquial; 'Grande estrondo' is MS1932's adjective without his supplied verb — number becomes size, which for the multitude of a sound is how Portuguese says it. v2 gate: the Latinist (minor) asked 'Multidão do som das águas'; held — see audit.

options.label: Grande estrondo das águas
options.note: v2: the stylist — 'muito estrondo' is colloquial ('what a racket'); still verbless, the mass of the sound kept as its greatness.

options.label: Muito estrondo das águas
options.note: Draft 1: quantity kept; heard as colloquial.

options.label: A multidão do estrondo das águas

decisions.why: vocem dare → fazer ouvir a voz (row, 17:14, 45:7: 'deu a sua voz' is not said). The Latin has no possessive here, and none is supplied. Subject first, as Portuguese orders it. v1: the Latinist asked 'deram voz' (dare), the stylist 'deram a sua voz'; both held for the row (17:14, 45:7), whose reason — 'dar a voz' is not Portuguese for making a sound, and 'dar voz a' means to voice something else — stands. The ambiguity reader heard 'the clouds thundered'.

decisions.why: transíre → passar (41:5 'passarei'); the Greek διαπορεύονται is 'go through, go about'. The present is kept (MS1932's past 'foram lançadas' is his). étenim → pois (row). sagítta → seta (row).

options.label: passam
options.note: Ruling: the plain verb of transíre.

decisions.why: in rota, 'in the wheel' (ἐν τῷ τροχῷ): the thunder rolls round like a wheel — the Latin's concrete image, kept (rule 5). DRB 'in a wheel'. MS1932 'a voz do teu trovão rolou' turns the image into a verb. The colon is verbless, as the Latin. tonítruum → trovão (103:7 a voce tonítrui tui will copy).

coruscátio → relâmpagos: the Greek is ἀστραπαί, the same word as 17:15 (fúlgura → relâmpagos) and as the near-twin 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura ejus orbi terræ, so by D15's test the two Latin nouns can share it, and 76:19 and 96:4 will read alike as the Greek does. orbis terræ → o mundo (D30). illúcere + dative, 'shone upon'; 'iluminaram o mundo' makes the dative an object (grammar), the subject first. The Latin's build is the option.

options.label: Os vossos relâmpagos iluminaram o mundo

options.label: Brilharam os vossos relâmpagos sobre o mundo

decisions.latin: Deduxísti sicut oves pópulum tuum, * in manu Móysi et Aaron.
decisions.why: dedúcere → guiar (D22). The natural order puts the object before the comparison; the Latin's order (the comparison first) is the option. Aaron → Aarão, as 117:3. in manu → pela mão (instrumental). The verse is also a responsory text (Quad4-0) and reads alone either way.

options.label: Guiastes o vosso povo como ovelhas, * pela mão de Moisés e de Aarão.

forms.order21: Guiastes o vosso povo como ovelhas, * pela mão de Moisés e de Aarão.

forms.order21: Guiastes como ovelhas o vosso povo, * pela mão de Moisés e de Aarão.

decisions.why: turbári → perturbar (row). The perfect passive of an inner state: 'fui perturbado' (118:60's form) is heard as someone else troubling the speaker (the v1 stylist); 'fiquei perturbado' says the state, and is still passive in build. Grammar, under D2.

déxtera → a direita (row, open; 17:36a, 15:11, 117:16 — the blind readers there heard the right hand first). The v1 stylist asks 'mão direita' (bare 'direita' = side, or politics); the ambiguity reader heard the hand but called it opaque. Held for the row, which binds many psalms; the option is here and the row notes the remark.

decisions.latin: quis Deus magnus sicut Deus noster?
decisions.why: 'Que Deus é grande' is heard first as the exclamation 'how great God is!' (the stylist and the ambiguity reader both). 'Qual' makes it a question from the first word; the same words otherwise. The versicle's response (Psalmi matutinum) reads alone from it.
The bare vocative 'Deus', as everywhere in the psalter (glossary; 50:3a). The v1 stylist asked 'ó Deus' for the pause; refused for the glossary's rule, kept as the option.

aquæ multæ without the article, as 28:3 'sobre muitas águas' and 17:17 'de muitas águas' (the phrase kept one across psalms, rule 6). The v1 stylist asked 'nas muitas águas' (the vast waters, not 'several waters'); kept as the option.

choices.76:2: The first colon is 3:5a word for word (identical Latin, rule 6). inténdere → atender (D3); the subject 'ele' is supplied so the verb does not open on a clitic. The second colon is verbless, as the Latin.
choices.76:3: décipere → enganar (row, which names this verse).
choices.76:5: v2 'fiquei perturbado' (decision `turbatus`); 76:17's 'se perturbaram' (of the abysses) follows 45:4's waters.
choices.76:6: cogitáre → pensar em (row). 'anos eternos' kept as the Latin's words (ἔτη αἰώνια), though they mean the years of old; MS1932 the same. v2 'tive em mente' (the stylist: the living idiom; draft 1 'tive na mente', MS1932) — the same words, the idiom's preposition.
choices.76:10: oblivísci + infinitive → esquecer-se de; miseréri → ter piedade (row).
choices.76:14: Verbless first half, as the Latin (see `insancto`). 'que Deus é grande como o nosso Deus?' — MS1932 has 'há'; the copula is the plainer. 'vós sois o Deus que fazeis maravilhas': the verb stays in the second person, as the Latin facis; the Matins antiphon 'Tu es Deus * qui facis mirabília' reads alone from it.
choices.76:15: notam fácere → fazer conhecer (row, 15:11); virtus → poder (row); redímere → resgatar (row, 30:6); in pópulis → entre os povos (56:10); in brácchio → com o braço (instrumental). Jacó, José.
choices.76:17: Verb first, with the enclitic, as the Latin's order and the responsory (Pasc4-0) have it. Bare vocative 'Deus' (the glossary's rule).
choices.76:19: The second colon copies 17:8a 'A terra se abalou e estremeceu' — identical Latin (Commóta est, et contrémuit terra), rule 6.
choices.76:20: Verbless, as the Latin and as 76:14 (the two verses are built alike). sémita → vereda (D15); in aquis multis → em muitas águas (28:3, 17:17); vestígia → pegadas (row); cognoscéntur, future passive → não serão conhecidas.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps076.md (no Diurnal: Ps 76 is not in the day hours). Hard readings: 76:3 mánibus meis nocte contra eum (verbless; ἐναντίον), 76:7 scopébam (search against sweep — L&S and the -ēbam form), 76:8 appónet ut complacítior sit adhuc, 76:14 in sancto (a place, by 76:20's parallel), 76:18 Multitúdo sónitus aquárum, 76:18b in rota. Formulas copied: 76:2a = 3:5a, 76:19b = 17:8a. The psalm has four liturgical texts that read alone (Matins antiphon 'Tu es Deus qui facis mirabília', versicle 76:14a / R. 76:14b, responsories 76:15, 76:17, 76:21) — each colon checked to stand by itself.

Hard pass. Soft, all accepted: 76:7b +4 (the exercéri row's 'me exercitava' and 'examinava' are long); 76:9b -6 (the formula 'de geração em geração'); 76:11a +3 (a supplied 'eu' was dropped to get there) and 76:11b +4 (the copula 'é' is needed); 76:14a +3 and 76:20a +3 (from +5 each after dropping a supplied copula 'está'); 76:18b(a) -3; 76:18 second colon +3 ('fizeram ouvir', the vocem dare row).
claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. Four minors, no major: 76:9 and 76:14 taken; 76:7 and 76:18 refused.

outcomes.reason: The form scopébam is an -ēbam imperfect, the conjugation of scopo, -ere (= σκοπέω, 'search'), which L&S gives for this very verse; the sweeping verb scopáre would make scopábam. The Greek ἔσκαλλεν is a searching verb. 'varria' (DRB) stays option 3.

outcomes.remark: in finem merged with 76:8 in ætérnum
'lugar' resolves the ambiguity of in sancto

outcomes.reason: The row vocem dare → fazer ouvir a voz (17:14, 45:7): 'deram voz' is heard as 'gave voice to' something.

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. 16 remarks in 13 verses; best 76:19, worst 76:13. Taken 8, refused 8 (each kept as an option).

outcomes.reason: exquírere → procurar (row; 26:8), kept apart from quǽrere → buscar; the gain is one syllable.

outcomes.remark: 'me exercitei' sounds like a gym (also 76:7, 76:13); 'me agitei'
outcomes.reason: The row across Ps 118 (five places) and 54:3; 'agitar-se' is another verb's meaning and the stylist has no form for 76:13. Not added as an option for that reason; the row's own option 'ocupar-se' is there.
